title: Evaluating the polypharmacological potential of cosmetic preservative Imidurea against Lung Cancer-associated EGFR, CDK2, STAT3, BCL2, p53, and ABCB1 proteins.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究化妆品防腐剂咪唑烷基脲对肺癌相关蛋白的多靶点抑制，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且未涉及TF-DNA结合或核酸体系，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: Lung cancer (LC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths globally, with both small and non-small cell lung cancer contributing to an estimated 1.80 million deaths annually. Drug resistance in LC treatment causes around 700,000 deaths globally and poses major economic challenges. While nearly 100 FDA-approved LC drugs exist, most target single proteins or pathways, making resistance more likely. There is an urgent need for multitargeted drugs that inhibit multiple pathways to reduce resistance and side effects. In this study, we examined 34 proteins from various LC-related pathways and prepared them for screening against the DrugBank library. Using high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS), standard precision (SP), and extra precision (XP) docking algorithms in Glide, we identified Imidurea (DB14075) as a promising multitargeted inhibitor. Docking scores ranged from -5.507 to -12.155 kcal/mol, and poses were refined through MM/GBSA calculations. Molecular fingerprinting was performed to analyse interaction patterns, and DFT and pharmacokinetics were assessed. Bonding angles were optimised to evaluate relative binding energy, followed by 100 ns MD simulations in water to assess stability and effectiveness. Imidurea showed strong multitargeted inhibitory effects across all 34 LC proteins, with docking scores between -5.507 and - 12.155 kcal/mol. MD simulations further supported its stability in binding to these targets. In MTT assays on A549 cells, Imidurea demonstrated dose-dependent anticancer effects, causing significant cell cycle arrest and cell death at 100 mug/mL. Imidurea is an affordable compound with promising multitargeted anticancer potential, particularly beneficial for developing nations and underprivileged groups. While these computational and in vitro MTT assays are encouraging, further detailed in vitro and in vivo studies are necessary to validate their efficacy and safety before clinical application.
abstract_zh: 肺癌（LC）仍是全球癌症相关死亡的主要原因之一，小细胞肺癌和非小细胞肺癌每年合计导致约180万人死亡。LC治疗中的耐药性在全球造成约70万人死亡，并带来重大经济挑战。尽管已有近100种FDA批准的LC药物，但大多数靶向单一蛋白质或通路，使得耐药性更易发生。迫切需要能够抑制多条通路的多靶点药物，以减少耐药性和副作用。在本研究中，我们考察了来自LC相关通路的34种蛋白质，并准备将其用于针对DrugBank库的筛选。利用Glide中的高通量虚拟筛选（HTVS）、标准精度（SP）和超精度（XP）对接算法，我们鉴定出咪脲（Imidurea，DB14075）作为一种有前景的多靶点抑制剂。对接分数范围为-5.507至-12.155 kcal/mol，并通过MM/GBSA计算优化了结合构象。进行了分子指纹分析以考察相互作用模式，并评估了DFT和药代动力学性质。优化了键角以评估相对结合能，随后在水中进行了100 ns的分子动力学（MD）模拟以评估稳定性和有效性。咪脲对所有34种LC蛋白质表现出强大的多靶点抑制效果，对接分数介于-5.507至-12.155 kcal/mol之间。MD模拟进一步支持其与这些靶点结合的稳定性。在A549细胞的MTT实验中，咪脲表现出剂量依赖性的抗癌效果，在100 μg/mL浓度下引起显著的细胞周期阻滞和细胞死亡。咪脲是一种经济实惠的化合物，具有显著的多靶点抗癌潜力，尤其对发展中国家和弱势群体有益。尽管这些计算和体外MTT实验结果令人鼓舞，但在临床应用前，仍需进一步的详细体外和体内研究以验证其有效性和安全性。
